title: His first recording and discographies
summary: His first recording was with Earl Hines in Chicago around 1933; he hopes Stanley Dance can help with his book.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: When was the first time you recorded?
The first time I recorded was with Earl Hines and that was in '33, about '33.
I don't know but I got the album home. We did it in Chicago. Yeah, we did. I forgot what label it was but I got the album home.
Do you know if there's -- do you have a
discography or do you know that there is one that chronicles most of the things that you've done, that shows --
Have you ever seen one of like Earl Hines or Jimmy Lunceford's recordings that would show most of the things you're on?
Stanley Dance has got one I'm sure.
Now he's supposed to have put together a good one on Earl.
But does he also have Lunceford and --
I think he has because I'm working on a book and he told me he's got a lot of things to help me. He's going to kind of put it together for me, you know.

So, he says I've got a lot of things, old pictures of you back there with Earl and everything, to put it together. He said I got more pictures than you'll ever dream of. So, I don't have them but he said he's got them, you know. I just got through talking to him about it. I'm going to do some tapes when I go back to Honolulu, you know.
